question:
Truncate or prevent overly-long sender addresses, for SES compatibility.

[Amazon SES](https://aws.amazon.com/ses/) has an (undocumented) limit on the size of address fields, and reject email with too-long `From` addresses, as follows:

```
Transaction failed: Address length is more than 320 bytes long: '=?utf-8?b?Zcy3zYLMvc2SzIrNjM2SzL3Ni8yIzYbNi82CzZ3Nhc2NzKfNmcygzLnMoMyuzK0=?= =?utf-8?b?zZPMocyizYfNiM2czKHMncykzJ94zLjMiMyFzJrNjM2dzL7Nis2SzILNis2gzYE=?= =?utf-8?b?zIfNhM2RzZjNksyBzZvNhsyPzIvMu8yezKjMp8yqzJ7Muc2czLNhzLfNisyIzL0=?= =?utf-8?b?zJXNoMyMzJrNkc2EzZ3Mi8yNzYDMjMy9zL7Mi82KzYrMh82DzZ3MjMyNzJLMn8yg?= =?utf-8?b?zLnMqsyjbcy0zZ3NisyUzJXMkMyZzLDMmcyizYXMusyizKDMrcyozY7Mrs2TzYc=?= =?utf-8?b?zK/MosyXzLvNhcyucMy3zIXMk82KzJrNg82YzJvNkcyIzZjNjM2MzL7Mvs2IzZk=?= =?utf-8?b?zKvMq8yezKTNnMyozYnMrcyvzKLMr8yWzJ3MucydzJ3MscyvzJbMoMy5zZRszLg=?= =?utf-8?b?zILMgcyPzIvMjM2AzIbMkMyCzYHMkMyEzI/Nks2YzZDMiMyIzIjMucywzKbMqs2V?= =?utf-8?b?zJ/MssyizLDNnMymzKvMs82UzK/Mu2XMuMyDzZDNhs2DzJvNm8yDzInMiM2bzJM=?= =?utf-8?b?zJXMv8yFzIXMkcyczJw=?= <example@example.com>'
```

This example header is the result of ["zalgo" text](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combining_character#Zalgo_text), and, when formatted, looks like:

```
From: ȩ̷̡̢̡͍͙̠̹̠̮̭͓͇͈̝̤̟͂̽͒̊͌͒̽͋̈͆͋͂͜͝ͅẍ̸̨̧̻̞̪̞̹̳̅͌̾͊͒̂͊́̇̈́͑͒́͛͆̏̋̚͘͜͝͠a̷̟̠̹̪̣͊̈̽̌͑̈́̋̍̀̌̽̾̋͊͊̇̓̌̍̒̕̚͠͝͝m̴̢̢̨̢̙̰̙̺̠̭͎̮͓͇̯̗̻̮͊̔̐̕͝ͅͅp̷̨̢̛͈͙̫̫̞̤͉̭̯̯̖̝̹̝̝̱̯̖̠̹͔̅̓͊̓͑̈͌͌̾̾̚͘͘͜l̸̢̹̰̦̪͕̟̲̰̦̫̳͔̯̻̂́̏̋̌̀̆̐̂́̐̄̏͒͐̈̈̈͘͜ẽ̸̛̜̜͐͆̓͛̃̉̈͛̓̿̅̅̑̕ <example@example.com>
```

This is bad because it results in dropped email notifications, and the users have no feedback as to why they are no longer receiving email from Zulip.

We have a couple options:
 1. Attempt to truncate the name before sending, such that the [RFC 2047](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2047)-encoded address is under 320 bytes.  This is potentially complicated, as we need to worry about not splitting multibyte characters mid-character, as well as dealing with combining characters; [this](https://stackoverflow.com/a/1820949) might be a possible starting point.
 2. Prevent such long names to begin with, at the UI level.  This may be a confusing requirement to explain to the user, since the "length" limit is in the _encoded_ form, which is non-trivial to understand for non-technical audiences.  It also would not address names that come in via e.g. LDAP import.

None of this would address with folks whose email address is `A <@example.com>`, however, since there's no way to truncate that.
issue_title: Truncate or prevent overly-long sender addresses, for SES compatibility.

question:
Make API for message edit history more friendly for clients

Currently, message edit history is a pain to work with, because the optimized data structure we use on the backend only records the **previous** stream and topic values.  What this means is you need to run effectively a reverse loop through the topics/streams if you ever want to compare the values, e.g. to determine if there's ever been a "resolve topic" transaction.  (You basically need to infer that the new topic is the `prev_subject` value of the next edit history event that has one, or if there isn't one, the current subject of the message).

Having thought about it a bit, I think the right way to fix this is as follows:
* First, add a database migration that does this loop once and changes the format of `message_edit_history` entries in the database to (A) be a Postgres JSONB field and (B) extend the existing edit history entries with `topic` and `new_stream_id` fields (name needs confirmation).  In that same migration, we can potentially take the opportunity to add a `prev_topic` field duplicating `prev_subject` (or maybe better, just switch over to `prev_topic` and then have a bit of code re-add `prev_subject` for clients), so that we're in a position to stop having the database have that legacy field name.
* We'd update the API documentation to document the new `prev_topic` and `new_stream_id` and `topic` fields.

Tagging as a release goal because I think changing this is the simplest path to completing #19919 via #21075, which cannot be done correctly at present without implementing the algorithm we want on the backend, on the frontend.

@cyphase FYI -- it'd be great if you can post the context for when you were working on this, since I think we'd picked names for the variables and the like.

@laurynmm perhaps you can take this up given your recent work with edit history, with @mateuszmandera available to support with the database migration part?
issue_title: Make API for message edit history more friendly for clients


``backend.populate_user`` will return None if the connection fails, causing user deactivation - because of the way the function is written in ``django_auth_ldap`` module. The only way the module gives us to "catch" such failures is by catching a signal it sends:

question:
Document /register data and events

For the mobile app, the most important part of the API that isn't documented is the data from the events system.

What does exist is some documentation of the high-level design, and documentation of how to invoke the two central endpoints [`/register`](https://zulipchat.com/api/register-queue) and [`/events`](https://zulipchat.com/api/get-events-from-queue). What's still needed is documentation of:
* the data returned by `/register`. This is a large data structure with lots of different fields and subfields.
* all the types of events, and the data they contain.

Among events, the most important single event type is `message`. There are a couple of examples of that one in the [GET `.../events` doc](https://zulipchat.com/api/get-events-from-queue). Those examples already show that `message.display_recipient` in such an event is kind of complicated, with a couple of different forms it can take. There are some other fields whose interpretation isn't obvious, too.

Then there are a bunch of other types of events too, of course, many of which are also important. I think the priority goes mostly in order of how frequent they are, because that's the major driver of how likely it'll matter if a client handles them wrong or even just hasn't implemented handling them. So the top of the priority list looks something like:
```
message
presence
typing
update_message_flags
update_message
delete_message
user_status
realm_user
```

One piece of this work is happening in #13499, which aims to make available a full set of programmatically generated examples.
issue_title: Document /register data and events

question:
GitHub bot should leave out issue description text on "issue assigned" events

Here's an [example message](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/243-mobile-team/topic/zulip-flutter/near/1517324) from the GitHub bot:

> gnprice assigned [issue #21 Push PerAccountRoot under MaterialApp, into each individual page widget](https://github.com/zulip/zulip-flutter/issues/21) (assigned to gnprice):
>
> > This will let us have a single MaterialApp that can navigate between pages that are for different accounts, as well as pages like the login flow and account-switch UI that are for no particular account at all. That makes it a necessity for doing #11 in a reasonable way.
> >
> > One part of this will be to let the PerAccountRoots for a given account all point to a single PerAccountStore. That's this TODO from #20 which I just sent:
> > ```dart
> >   // TODO add a registry of [PerAccountStore]s, like the latter's of [MessageListView]
> >   //   That will allow us to have many [PerAccountRoot] widgets for a given
> >   //   account, e.g. at the top of each page; and to access server data from
> >   //   outside any [PerAccountRoot], e.g. for handling a notification.
> > ```
> >
> > The other part to take care of will be arranging that the API we provide for ourselves to use when we're adding new routes, and navigating to routes, isn't too annoying or error-prone. I have some thoughts and we'll see how it looks after I experiment.

That would be about right for the "issue created" event. But this isn't that — it's the "issue assigned" event. The description — those multiple paragraphs of prose plus code — isn't something that is new or changed, or ever will be on this type of event. So it should be omitted.

In particular this event will commonly come immediately after the "issue created" event, which means the description gets posted twice in a row.

I don't know what the bot currently does on "PR assigned" events, but the same thing applies there: it should not include the PR description text.
issue_title: GitHub bot should leave out issue description text on "issue assigned" events

question:
Soft reactivate users who sending them an email or push notification

Zulip has this great [soft deactivation](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/sending-messages.html#soft-deactivation) feature, which makes a huge difference in the performance of sending messages in organizations with 10Ks of inactive users.

However, one problem that it has is that it can be a somewhat bad experience to come back from soft deactivation with 50K+ unreads, sometimes resulting in 500s the first time the user tries to load the page, because soft reactivation can take up to a minute or so and it's possible for that to hit a timeout.  We need to fix that loading experience (), but separately, we should also try to avoid that happening.

It's fairly common that a user returns to a Zulip community where they've been inactive after a long absence due to a private message or mention received in that community.  So I propose the following:
* When a user who is currently `long_term_idle` has an email or mobile push notification triggered not due to a user_group or wildcard mention, we push an event into the `deferred_work` [queue processor](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/subsystems/queuing.html) with `type="soft_reactivate"`.
* The `deferred_work` queue processor handler for that event type should call `reactivate_user_if_soft_deactivated`.

We want to exclude wildcard mentions, because otherwise a single wildcard mention would fill this queue with every user in the organization, many of whom are unlikely to click in, but in any case would defeat the disk storage benefits of soft deactivation in a community that ever did wildcard mentions.  For user group mentions -- I think I'd want this feature if the group had <10 members, not not if it was larger; I'm not sure how hard the plumbing would be to support that, so I'd do a first version excluding group mentions entirely, and then iterate from there.

@abhijeetbodas2001 @ryanreh99 FYI; it's possible this would be a very fast little project for you, since you know the relevant code paths really well at the moment.
issue_title: Soft reactivate users who sending them an email or push notification

question:
OpenAPI definitions incorrectly encode array and object parameters

According to the [OpenAPI specification](https://swagger.io/specification/), a parameter like

```yaml
      - name: messages
        in: query
        description: An array containing the IDs of the target messages.
        schema:
          type: array
          items:
            type: integer
        example: [4, 8, 15]
        required: true
```

should actually serialize as `messages=4,8,15` rather than `messages=[4, 8, 15]`. Since we’re expecting the latter, this parameter should have been defined as

```yaml
      - name: messages
        in: query
        description: An array containing the IDs of the target messages.
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              type: array
              items:
                type: integer
        required: true
```

I’m not sure whether whether the `example` should be written `[4, 8, 15]` or `"[4, 8, 15]"` (or perhaps it should be `[4, 8, 15]` but indented to be a child of `schema`).

The current `test_openapi` doesn’t accept this, so it needs to be fixed to accept the correct definition and ideally reject the incorrect one.
issue_title: OpenAPI definitions incorrectly encode array and object parameters

question:
Create UserMessage rows for outgoing webhook and embedded bots

As reported in [this CZO thread](https://chat.zulip.org/#narrow/stream/9-issues/topic/Bot.20does.20not.20add.20an.20emoji.20reaction.20to.20a.20message/near/1732692), outgoing webhook bots fail `has_message_access` checks for messages that they should have access to, because they don't have a `UserMessage` row for them. We originally didn't create those as a performance optimization. We could change `has_message_access` and related code to make that check pass, but I think that's a road of weird invariant violations that may be hard to manage; I suppose the best option in that space would be to treat them like `long_term_idle` users.

Since the documentation on https://zulip.com/help/bots-overview claims that outgoing webhooks have the rights/permissions of a generic bot, and I believe that's how things are enforced in the API, I think the most correct solution is to just create `UserMessage` rows for outgoing webhook bots, just like we would any other user. We may want to, as a follow-up, create a more limited class of outgoing-webhook bot that only gets `UserMessage` rows for messages that it is going to be notified for, but that's not the promise of "works like a generic bot". See #28870 for a proposal for adding a more limited outgoing webhook bot type.

It could be a nice touch to also have message flags keep track of whether the outgoing webhook in fact processed the message. That would involve something like the following:

* Stop filtering service bots in `get_recipient_info`.
* Move the call of `get_service_bot_events` before `create_user_messages` so its conclusions can be used there.
* In `create_user_messages`, decide whether the `read` flag should be initially set when creating a `UserMessage` for an outgoing webhook bot based on whether we're planning for that message to be processed as an outgoing webhook based on the `get_service_bot_events` calculation. Or maybe we should use a new flag along the lines of `active_mobile_push_notification`; deserves discussion.
* Set the `read` (or whatever) flag once the appropriate queue worker has processed them (`EmbeddedBotWorker` or `OutgoingWebhookWorker`, as appropriate).

@PIG208 FYI since you had worked around this a different way in #18117, and may have thoughts on this.
issue_title: Create UserMessage rows for outgoing webhook and embedded bots

question:
Fix recursive exceptions from _RateLimitFilter

We have a very useful piece of code, `_RateLimitFilter`, which is designed to avoid sending us a billion error emails in the event that a Zulip production server is down in a way that throws the same exception a lot.  The code uses memcached to ensure we send each traceback roughly once per Zulip server per 10 minutes (or if memcached is unavailable, at most 1/process/10 minutes, since we use memcached to coordinate between processes)

There are a few problems with it:
(1) There are no tests, which makes iterating on the code a risky option.
(2) If memcached is down, there end up being some `logging.error` calls internal to the Django/memcached setup that happen inside the `cache.set()` call, and those aren't caught by the `except Exception` block around it.  This ends up resulting in infinite recursion, eventually leading to `Fatal Python error: Cannot recover from stack overflow.`, since this handler is configured to run for `logging.error` in addition to `logging.exception`.

We should fix this as follows:
* Eliminate the "infinite recursion" problem by adding an outer try/finally block that sets a global (or maybe thread-local?) variable `handling_exception = True` at the start, and sets it back to false at the end.
* Add unit tests that can reproduce this error condition (I think basically we just need to `mock.patch` the `cache.get` call to either throw an exception or do a `logging.error` call for the main corner cases)
* Let's look at the actual `logging.error` message Django gives when memcached is down; I have a recollection that it has a large random ID in it, which makes the duplicate-filtering we use not work at all.
issue_title: Fix recursive exceptions from _RateLimitFilter
